sentences.text: Kwangsisaurus is an extinct basal pistosauroid reptile that lived during the Triassic period.
The genus contains a single species, Kwangsisaurus orientalis, which was named by Yang Zhongjian in 1965.
Its name combines the old designation for Guangxi with the Greek word for lizard, emphasizing its East Asian origin.
The only known specimen is a fragmentary postcranial skeleton held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
This holotype includes twenty back vertebrae, six front tail vertebrae, a damaged shoulder girdle, and the right forelimb.
The original describer incorrectly oriented the bones by mistaking the neck for a tail and the shoulder for a pelvis.
The fossil was collected from the Beisi Formation of the Loulou Group at Fupingtun in Guangxi Province.
Scientists debate whether this animal lived in the Early or Middle Triassic.
